summary.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin hit 5%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (like-for-like 40%), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like against a 13.8% underlying pharma market. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% to INR52 crore, while PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 23% revenue growth excluding new acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said it would revisit guidance after H1.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand-fulfilment; gross margin gains here attributed to scale-driven procurement efficiencies. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited to release working capital; that exit reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to cross INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than pharma; company plays a demand-generation (commercial) role here. Management said it is comfortably above INR1,000 crore for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: ~23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions), 5% EBITDA margin, 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.
Management said it is tracking to or above the 5% margin guidance and may revise it after H1 FY27 if H2 looks better; no revision to working capital guidance after Q1.

Medium-term: management says it can grow above 20% over 3-4 years, organic-led, and modelling assumption of 20% is a safe base; ROCE target 25-30% in that period; internal EBITDA margin aspiration above 6%.
Interest cost expected broadly flat QoQ in the same range (not significantly lower) after ~INR200 crore acquisition debt taken around late Jan/early Feb.
Employee cost increments mostly hit in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major further increase expected. Effective tax rate guidance for FY27 is 22.5%; FY28+ guidance to come near FY27 close.
Depreciation run-rate in Q1 expected to continue, subject to any major new capex.
Acquisitions: no major deals planned in FY27, though pipeline exists and openness to deals in Q4 FY27; minority call options exercisable over 2-5 years, not falling due entirely in FY27.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q4 included one-time catch-up on certain machines; Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate absent major capex.
Capital deployment: surplus OCF could go to acquisitions, debt reduction or buying out minorities; no dividend planned. Management will compare which option most improves EPS.
Subsidiaries were funded via intercompany loans; these are being pulled back to fund parent-level deployment.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (from 7-9% earlier), driven by volume growth turning positive across therapy areas; management could not isolate a specific cause and declined to forecast IPM.

Entero's outperformance is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range (3,000+ principals) and an all-India network; wallet share growth is said to exceed new-customer growth.
MedTech: limited distributor competition and scope for national-level collaborations; management targets ~20% MedTech growth over 3-5 years.
Pharma categories served: patented drugs, branded generics and trade generics; not pure generics. Management says 98-99% of Indian pharma sits in these segments.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 due to government (diagnostic PPP) billing preponement, which lifted the Q1 inorganic comparison base effect.

qa_highlights.question: What growth can Entero achieve over 3-5 years with no acquisitions, and what ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets over 20% growth in the near term (3-4 years), organic and inorganic combined, and says ROCE could reach 25-30% in that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the minority interest large and how are the call options structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority stakes come from majority buyouts with pre-agreed call options at the original acquisition multiple, exercisable over 2-5 years; minority share is reinvested, not paid out. Funding route (holdco or subsidiary) is not defined by contract.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inorganic revenue contribution fall QoQ from ~26% to ~20.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of Q1 revenue was pulled into Q4 FY26 due to government project billing preponement ahead of budget closure, creating a high base.

qa_highlights.question: Are one-off Q4 items in other opex recurring, and is ~INR55 crore run-rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the INR11.5 crore one-offs, only part went to other expenses; part went to gross margin. Management said the INR55 crore other opex run-rate is sustainable at this level.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 60 bps sequential margin improvement and is further expansion expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 had one-offs that depressed margin; excluding them Q4 was near 5%. Management aims to improve margins further but maintains 5% full-year guidance, with possible upgrade after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company generate enough internal cash to fund growth and reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF defined as EBITDA less working capital change; management targets 50% of EBITDA as OCF on an annual basis. Surplus could fund debt reduction, acquisitions or minority buyouts; quarterly OCF and balance sheet data to be disclosed in September.

risks_watch: Quarterly revenue timing: government billing preponement shifted revenue between Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; watch the inorganic and reported growth base effects.
Rising non-controlling interest (INR14-17 crore per quarter) and call options over 2-5 years may require funding at holdco or subsidiary level; funding route not defined.
Debt: ~INR200 crore acquisition borrowing; interest cost to stay roughly flat; net debt and gross debt not disclosed for Q1.
IPM growth shift to double digits has no identified cause; management declined to forecast whether it will persist.
Deferred tax assets present; FY27 tax rate guidance 22.5% versus normalised 25% expected by some analysts; FY28 guidance pending.
Exit of low-margin sub-distribution accounts continues and may reduce reported growth further.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on margins, growth and returns, with clear guidance maintained. Evasive on IPM growth drivers and on funding of minority buyouts, and deferred quarter-level balance sheet and OCF detail to September.
key_quotes: We are pleased to have delivered our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the very first quarter of the year.
This is a clear evidence that our growth is combined with capital efficiency.
So, just because you are OCF positive means you have enough internal accrual to fund your working capital changes.
We should not be looking at OCF on a quarter-to-quarter basis. We should be looking at an annual basis.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation) and 5% EBITDA margin was reiterated; backing is wallet-share gains and MedTech demand-generation with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 5.0% (+143 bps YoY) and gross margin 11.4% (+147 bps) on procurement scale; management says it is tracking to or above the 5% FY27 guide and aims to improve further, with Q4 one-offs having depressed margin.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like vs 13.8% pharma market, with FY27 guide of ~23% ex-acquisitions held and wallet-share gains cited; no volume figures given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Depreciation run-rate expected flat absent major capex and surplus OCF is earmarked for acquisitions, debt reduction or minority buyouts rather than capex; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is tracking to or above 5% margin and said it may revisit guidance after H1 if H2 looks better; a revenue upgrade is not explicitly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of ~23% growth, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% OCF conversion was reiterated and Q1 margin already at 5.0%; risks are timing-related (billing preponement, sub-distribution exits ~2.5pt growth drag) rather than a cut.

rows.label: MedTech crossing INR1,000 crore in FY27
rows.why: Organic MedTech revenue is on track and management says it is comfortably above INR1,000 crore for the full year, with higher margins than pharma and a ~20% growth target over 3-5 years.

rows.label: Surplus OCF to debt reduction or minority buyouts
rows.why: Surplus OCF could go to debt reduction, acquisitions or minority buyouts (INR14 crore NCI per quarter), but funding route is undefined and quarterly OCF and balance sheet detail is deferred to September.

rows.label: Minority call option exercises
rows.why: Call options at original acquisition multiples are exercisable over 2-5 years, not falling due entirely in FY27, and NCI runs INR14-17 crore per quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, growth and returns and reiterated FY27 guidance, but was evasive on IPM drivers and on how minority buyouts will be funded; analysts pushed on the Q4 billing pull-forward, one-off opex and sustainability of the INR55 crore other opex run-rate.
